api/EditSharp.Caching.Proxy.ProxyCache.h.title: Class ProxyCache | EditSharp
api/EditSharp.Caching.Proxy.ProxyCache.h.summary: Class ProxyCache Namespace EditSharp.Caching.Proxy Assembly EditSharp.dll Builds and finds proxies: one per original media file, used for scrubbing, playback and editing. public static class ProxyCache Inheritance object ProxyCache Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks An original is identified by a hash of its content, so a renamed, moved or copied file finds the same proxy. Nothing builds automatically: call BuildAsync(string, ProxyFormat?, IProgress<double>?, HardwareAccelerator, CancellationToken) (typically on import) and watch StatusChanged; everything that reads media only looks proxies up. A proxy can be read up to AvailableUpTo while it builds, stays readable if the build is interrupted, and the next build resumes it. Building a different format replaces the proxy: the old one serves reads until the new one completes, then is deleted. Proxies live under ProxyDirectory, in a folder named after the first two characters of the hash. Each format has its own file stem (hash.delta7, .rgba, .dnxhr, .prores): .esrp proxies are one .esrp file, and MOV proxies are a .mov.json sidecar plus numbered segments while building and one .mov once complete. Methods BuildAsync(string, ProxyFormat?, IProgress<double>?, HardwareAccelerator, CancellationToken) Builds a file's proxy, resuming a partial one of the same format, and finishes when it's complete. public static Task<ProxyEntry> BuildAsync(string sourcePath, ProxyFormat? format = null, IProgress<double>? progress = null, HardwareAccelerator hwAccel = HardwareAccelerator.GPU, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters sourcePath string The original media file. format ProxyFormat? The format to build; null for ProxyFormat. progress IProgress<double> Receives the build's progress, 0 to 1. hwAccel HardwareAccelerator Whether decoding the original may use the GPU. ct CancellationToken Detaches this caller from the build. Returns Task<ProxyEntry> The complete proxy. Remarks Finishes at once if a complete proxy in that format exists. Several callers asking for the same file share one build. Cancelling only detaches this caller; the build stops when no caller is left, and what it wrote stays readable and resumable. Exceptions FileNotFoundException sourcePath doesn't exist. OperationCanceledException ct was cancelled. GetStatusAsync(string, CancellationToken) Where a file's proxy stands, from running builds first and then the disk. public static Task<ProxyStatus> GetStatusAsync(string sourcePath, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters sourcePath string The original media file. ct CancellationToken Cancels hashing the file. Returns Task<ProxyStatus> The proxy's status; NotCached when there is none. Exceptions FileNotFoundException sourcePath doesn't exist. IsBuilding(string) Whether a build of a file's proxy is queued or running in this process. public static bool IsBuilding(string sourcePath) Parameters sourcePath string The original media file. Returns bool Whether a build is queued or running. Remarks Answers from memory without waiting; a file this process hasn't hashed yet reads as not building. TryGetAsync(string, CancellationToken) Finds a file's proxy on disk, complete or partial. public static Task<ProxyEntry?> TryGetAsync(string sourcePath, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters sourcePath string The original media file. ct CancellationToken Cancels hashing the file. Returns Task<ProxyEntry> The proxy, or null when there is none. Remarks Afterwards TryGetEntry(string, out ProxyEntry) answers for the same unchanged file without waiting. Exceptions FileNotFoundException sourcePath doesn't exist. Returns bool Whether the proxy is known. Remarks Known means found by TryGetAsync(string, CancellationToken), GetStatusAsync(string, CancellationToken) or a build. Frames are composited in order on the GPU and written straight into ffmpeg's stdin as raw RGBA; audio is rendered by the streaming audio engine at the same time and written into a named pipe ffmpeg reads as its second input. Neither ever touches disk before it's encoded. Sources are read ahead of the frame being composited, and each clip's decoder is closed once the clip has passed.
